extracted.intended_audience: members of the public, activists, and supporters who will submit public comments or testify at government hearings
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for drafting and delivering public comments and short hearing testimony for federal rulemaking and administrative proceedings, emphasizing both personal stories and technical/legal submissions to create a robust Administrative Record.

rubrics_metrics.name: In-depth, technical comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Attorneys research and write in-depth, technical comments detailing how regulations could and should be stronger to protect the environment, communities, and the planet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technical/legal comments preserve grounds for litigation and help agencies see specific regulatory changes; these are complementary to personal comments and should be substantive and detailed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personal stories matter for building the human record
rubrics_metrics.description: Your specific experiences, knowledge, and voice are crucial to add to the Administrative Record through the comment periods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Personal stories and specific impacts on you or your community add unique value; include specific dates and places where relevant to make testimony and comments more resonant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Both individual citizen comments AND organizational technical comments are needed
rubrics_metrics.description: Individual personal comments and organizational technical/legal comments play different but complementary roles in rulemaking and potential later litigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit both types when possible: individuals provide human impacts; organizations provide detailed legal/technical analysis that preserves grounds for court challenges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comments must enter the docket to count (exhaustion principle)
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments must be submitted to the agency docket to be part of the Administrative Record and to be available for later judicial review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Courts can only look at documents in the Administrative Record—including public comments—so it is essential that comments are properly docketed during the comment period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand the legal framework (NEPA, APA, and rulemaking process)
rubrics_metrics.description: Statutes like the National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA) and the Administrative Procedure Act (APA) require agencies to ask the public to weigh in before adopting or changing regulations, and comments are collected at various points in the process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this framework to know when and how to submit comments; these laws create the procedural basis that makes public comments meaningful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sign up in advance for public hearings
rubrics_metrics.description: For oral testimony at hearings, sign up ahead of time so you are scheduled to speak.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Early sign-up helps ensure you get a chance to speak and that organizers can manage time and order of speakers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prepare a 1–2 minute statement for hearings
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep oral testimony short—prepare a concise 1–2 minute statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Brevity increases impact and fits typical hearing time limits; focus your prepared remarks on your strongest point(s).

rubrics_metrics.name: Lead with your strongest point
rubrics_metrics.description: Begin oral testimony or written comments by stating your most important point up front.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Audiences and agency reviewers remember the lead; put the clearest, strongest message first to maximize influence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include specific dates/places in personal testimony
rubrics_metrics.description: Personal stories with specific dates and places resonate and strengthen the factual record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concrete details make impacts more credible and useful for the Administrative Record and for agency consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Yield extra time to other commenters with similar concerns
rubrics_metrics.description: If multiple people share the same concerns, consider yielding your remaining time to let others speak.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is courteous hearing etiquette and helps broaden the range of voices presented when time is limited.
